applicabilityBasis.summary: The current Royal product page describes a USD-referenced token for payment, settlement and treasury uses, with authorized-participant minting and redemption subject to published programme conditions.

genius.notes: Reviewed October 7, 2026. Retain the payment-stablecoin assessment and bounded no-public-authorization finding. The August 28 registry describes RUSD as launch preparation and says its legal issuer, redemption terms and reserves will be published later. It identifies RIB Digital as technology infrastructure and disclaims ribg.digital as current authority. The product page lists deployment addresses matching the delisted Pharos asset but leaves issuer details blank. Restore the pre-sweep issuerEntity RIB Digital Holdings Limited and Hong Kong domicile for the historical delisted asset. The reopened April 2026 RUSD whitepaper cover identifies The RIB Digital Holdings Limited, Hong Kong, and the viewer configuration links the tracked Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and TRON contracts. The newer launch-preparation registry does not establish a change of issuer for the historical token; the mapping to the planned current programme remains unresolved. reserveDisclosurePresent and redemptionPolicyPresent refer only to a published reserve/redemption framework, not verified current balances or an unconditional holder redemption right. No current monthly attestation was located. The legacy FlipHTML5 text reader exposed only a shell, but the linked whitepaper cover image was reopened directly and its issuer statement was readable. The earlier review reported HTTP 404 at the linked rib.digital transparency URL. GENIUS primary issuer requirements remain pre-effective; Treasury describes expected January 18, 2027 effectiveness and the general DASP prohibition from July 18, 2028. Foreign issuer qualification cannot be determined without a verified issuer.
